overal.goal: Renaming a command template repoints every task that uses it (in every project, running ones included) by saving the task files directly, without the task lock. A running task can lose its own writes, or the repoint can be overwritten by the runner. Do the repoint through the task store's modify under the lock, and skip or defer running tasks (a running task keeps its own copy of the instructions anyway). Found in the phase 5 review of the Automation page (2026-11-02).

rules.do: Read docs/boof-runner.md (command templates) and the rename code in packages/api/src/ops/admin.ts before changing code.
Write a failing test first: a rename while a task using the template is running must not touch that task's file, and the other tasks must still be repointed.
Run `npm run typecheck && npm test` and `npm run lint` before finishing.
rules.dont: Do not change public API or MCP shapes without updating docs/api.md and the OpenAPI document.
Do not commit secrets, data roots or build output.

versions.version: Filed from the phase 5 Task 6 review (2026-11-02); not started.

renameCommand repoints each task through TaskStore.modify under the task lock; a running task (checked again under the lock, so one that starts mid-rename is caught) is left unwritten and listed in the new optional skippedTasks of the PUT /commands/{id} result. Tests: running and racing tasks.

Review follow-ups (M1, M4): a rename repoints only tasks that can still run (draft, pending, action, stopped, failed) and leaves done and archived tasks as they are; a task that leaves running, or is retried or unarchived, drops a command id whose template no longer exists and keeps its copied instructions (clearMissingCommand).

tests.strategy: Service test with the mock tool: rename a template used by a pending and a running task; the pending one is repointed under the lock, the running one is left alone.
